1	# Configuration reference
2	
3	`.agent-context/config.yaml` is canonical, reviewed project data. The copied
4	`.agent-context/config.schema.json` is generated editor support and is repaired by `carrylog sync`.
5	
6	## Version contract
7	
8	Configuration versions `1` and `2` are supported. Configuration version and npm package version are
9	separate; unknown versions and cross-version adapter names fail before any write.
10	
11	Version 1 is the frozen published compatibility contract. Version 2 adds universal agent surfaces and
12	continuity policy. New initialization creates v2, while existing v1 repositories remain valid and are
13	never rewritten implicitly. See [ADR-0005](decisions/0005-configuration-v1-compatibility.md) and
14	[ADR-0009](decisions/0009-configuration-v2-and-universal-surfaces.md).
15	
16	Every runtime-decoder-accepted configuration also passes its versioned public JSON Schema. JSON
17	Schema validation alone is insufficient: runtime checks additionally enforce normalized ownership,
18	checkpoint references, portable paths, symlink rejection, actual content budgets, and filesystem
19	state.
20	
21	The recommended first line enables YAML editor validation:
22	
23	```yaml
24	# yaml-language-server: $schema=./config.schema.json
25	```
26	
27	An older v1 file without this comment remains valid at runtime. `validate` emits
28	`W_CONFIG_SCHEMA_HEADER`; add the comment manually after review. `sync` does not rewrite canonical
29	YAML.
30	
31	## Fields
32	
33	### `version`
34	
35	Required integer. Must be `1` or `2`.
36	
37	### `project.name`
38	
39	Required single-line string, 1–120 Unicode characters. Leading/trailing whitespace and reserved
40	managed-marker text are rejected.
41	
42	### `documents`
43	
44	Required array with 1–256 entries and at least one `load: always` entry.
45	
46	| Field | Contract |
47	| --- | --- |
48	| `id` | Unique lowercase identifier matching `[a-z][a-z0-9-]*`, at most 64 characters |
49	| `path` | Unique path relative to `.agent-context/`, at most 1024 Unicode characters |
50	| `load` | `always` or `on-demand` |
51	| `description` | Single-line router description, at most 240 characters |
52	| `triggers` | Optional non-empty list of at most 32 single-line strings, each at most 120 characters |
53	
54	Document path uniqueness uses conservative Unicode compatibility and multi-step case normalization
55	for cross-platform safety. This can intentionally reject names that coexist on one filesystem when
56	another supported filesystem may alias them.
57	
58	Version 1 uses document ID `handoff` for `carrylog handoff`. Version 2 uses
59	`continuity.checkpointDocument`, whose target must exist and use `load: always`.
60	
61	The complete instructions template published in `@jaemani/agent-context-kit@0.1.0-beta.3` defines
62	the old-package-to-Carrylog migration boundary independently of a mutable document ID or path.
63	Carrylog can replace that exact template while
64	preserving LF or CRLF line endings. Customized always-loaded context with a command-shaped invocation
65	of the removed `ackit` executable is invalid until a maintainer reviews and changes the command;
66	historical prose and other human content are not inferred from a template.
67	
68	### `adapters`
69	
70	Required array with 1–32 entries.
71	
72	| Field | Contract |
73	| --- | --- |
74	| `type` | v1: `codex` or `claude`; v2: `agents`, `claude`, or `gemini` |
75	| `output` | Unique project-relative instruction-file path |
76	
77	The v2 `agents` surface is shared by Codex and Cursor and defaults to `AGENTS.md`; this avoids two
78	logical harnesses competing for one output. `claude` defaults to `CLAUDE.md`, and `gemini` defaults to
79	`GEMINI.md`.
80	
81	### `continuity` (v2 only)
82	
83	| Field | Contract |
84	| --- | --- |
85	| `checkpointDocument` | ID of one configured `load: always` document |
86	| `generateSkills` | Generate and validate the shared `.agents` Skill and Claude adapter Skill |
87	
88	When Skill generation is disabled, existing Carrylog-marked Skills are not deleted automatically;
89	`validate` warns so their removal remains an explicit reviewed action.
90	
91	The generated continuity Skill resolves executables offline in a fixed order: a compatible Carrylog
92	source build, the nearest compatible project-pinned package, then a compatible global installation.
93	Each selected candidate must support `resume`; an incompatible pinned candidate stops with explicit
94	guidance instead of falling through or downloading another version.
95	
96	Every config, document, copied schema, and adapter output has exclusive path ownership. Exact,
97	case-folded, or Unicode-normalized collisions fail before planning writes.
98	
99	### `policies`
100	
101	- `maxAlwaysCharacters`: total JavaScript character units allowed across `always` documents;
102	- `maxAdapterCharacters`: maximum generated managed block per adapter.
103	
104	Both are required integers from 1,000 through 100,000. These deterministic budgets are not claims
105	about a particular model tokenizer. Independently of those configurable rendering budgets, portable
106	resume observes at most 8 MiB across the configuration and all canonical documents in one pass. This
107	fixed aggregate read limit prevents a large on-demand catalog from multiplying per-file limits into
108	unbounded retained memory.
109	
110	## Portable path rules
111	
112	Paths use `/`, remain relative and normalized, and cannot contain `.`/`..` segments, empty segments,
113	NUL/control characters, Windows-reserved names/characters, trailing dots/spaces, or reserved marker
114	text. Existing symlink components are rejected. A valid-looking schema path can still fail runtime
115	ownership or filesystem checks.
116	
117	## Explicit v1 migration
118	
119	```bash
120	carrylog migrate --to 2 --universal --dry-run
121	carrylog migrate --to 2 --universal
122	carrylog validate
123	```
124	
125	Without `--universal`, migration preserves the selected v1 surfaces and leaves Skill generation
126	disabled. With it, Carrylog ensures `agents`, `claude`, and `gemini` surfaces and enables Skills. A
127	stock v1 handoff can be converted automatically; customized prose must already satisfy the checkpoint
128	section contract or migration stops with `E_CHECKPOINT_REVIEW_REQUIRED`.
129	
130	Migration preserves YAML comments and LF/CRLF style, preflights all outputs, and writes config last.
131	`--check` exits 1 when migration work remains; `--dry-run` prints the plan without writing.
132	
133	`sync`, `validate`, `handoff`, `checkpoint`, `migrate`, and `resume` discover the nearest
134	`.agent-context/config.yaml` while walking upward from the explicit or current root. They can
135	therefore run from a nested project directory. `init` treats its explicit or current root as the new
136	project root and does not perform upward discovery.
137	
138	## Version 2 example
139	
140	```yaml
141	# yaml-language-server: $schema=./config.schema.json
142	version: 2
143	project:
144	  name: Example service
145	documents:
146	  - id: handoff
147	    path: handoff.md
148	    load: always
149	    description: Verified portable checkpoint and next action
150	  - id: architecture
151	    path: architecture.md
152	    load: on-demand
153	    description: System boundaries and module responsibilities
154	    triggers:
155	      - architecture changes
156	adapters:
157	  - type: agents
158	    output: AGENTS.md
159	  - type: claude
160	    output: CLAUDE.md
161	  - type: gemini
162	    output: GEMINI.md
163	continuity:
164	  checkpointDocument: handoff
165	  generateSkills: true
166	policies:
167	  maxAlwaysCharacters: 16000
168	  maxAdapterCharacters: 12000
169	```

1	# ADR-0010: Define continuity as a portable checkpoint and verified resume envelope
2	
3	- Status: Accepted
4	- Date: 2026-07-11
5	- Owners: Repository maintainer
6	
7	## Context
8	
9	Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, and Gemini CLI have different private session stores, native resume
10	commands, transcript formats, and compaction behavior. Parsing those stores would couple Carrylog to
11	undocumented machine-local state, risk exporting secrets or hidden reasoning, and still would not
12	reconstruct another provider's internal model state.
13	
14	The portable need is narrower: a fresh agent must recover the reviewed objective, completed work,
15	verification, decisions, risks, next action, stable project context, and current repository evidence.
16	
17	## Decision
18	
19	Carrylog's continuity boundary is repository-owned, reviewable state plus a fresh bounded Git
20	observation. It does not promise conversation replay or control over provider compaction.
21	
22	A v2 checkpoint contains these H2 sections exactly once and in order: `Objective`, `Completed`,
23	`Verification`, `Decisions`, `Risks`, and `Next action`. Bodies must be non-empty. Headings inside
24	managed Git evidence, fenced code, blockquotes, or indented code are not section declarations.
25	`carrylog checkpoint` is the continuity-oriented alias for the existing narrative-preserving handoff
26	evidence refresh; `handoff` remains compatible.
27	
28	`carrylog resume --json` emits format version 1 with:
29	
30	- project name, configuration version, portable config path, and raw-byte SHA-256;
31	- parsed checkpoint sections, digest, and Git-evidence staleness;
32	- a projected Git snapshot without commit timestamps;
33	- full always-loaded context except the separately represented checkpoint;
34	- metadata-only on-demand catalog entries with triggers and digests;
35	- deterministic diagnostics, including `W_CHECKPOINT_STALE`.
36	
37	The envelope omits absolute roots, session identifiers, raw transcripts, hidden reasoning, provider
38	databases, and wall-clock freshness claims. `--check` exits 1 when checkpoint Git evidence is stale.
39	
40	Before export, Carrylog validates the project, reads config and every canonical document through
41	regular-file handles, rejects symlinks and hard links, verifies handle/path inode identity and
42	size/mtime before and after each bounded UTF-8 read, observes Git, then repeats the config/document
43	observation. It accepts only two matching observations and retries the complete envelope at most
44	three times. The exact observed document bytes are revalidated before serialization.
45	
46	Generated Skills contain only this maintenance protocol, never project content. Codex, Cursor, and
47	Gemini CLI share `.agents/skills/carrylog-continuity/SKILL.md`; Claude Code receives a minimal
48	`.claude/skills` adapter that points to the canonical Skill. Skill ownership requires exactly one
49	standalone marker. The Skill uses a global executable, a verified local `node_modules/.bin` package,
50	or the built CLI only inside Carrylog's own source repository; it never installs or upgrades a package
51	implicitly. An MCP server may later expose the same read model, but Markdown and CLI output remain the
52	baseline.
53	
54	## Rejected alternatives
55	
56	- **One universal raw transcript file:** rejected because providers do not share a stable transcript
57	  or hidden-state contract and transcripts can contain credentials and irrelevant tool output.
58	- **Parse provider JSONL, SQLite, or native resume stores:** rejected as private, machine-local, and
59	  version-fragile.
60	- **Let a model summarize automatically during resume:** rejected because deterministic validation
61	  cannot verify a new semantic summary and core runtime must remain offline.
62	- **Copy all on-demand documents into every envelope:** rejected because it defeats progressive
63	  disclosure and inflates startup context.
64	- **Claim control over native compaction:** rejected because Carrylog operates outside provider
65	  context-window implementations.
66	
67	## Consequences
68	
69	- Native same-provider resume and Carrylog resume are complementary: native resume may recover a
70	  conversation; Carrylog recovers durable cross-provider project state.
71	- One-off `npx` initialization does not provide a future executable. Automated resume requires a
72	  project-pinned or global Carrylog install; manual Markdown reading remains available without it.
73	- Agents and maintainers remain responsible for accurate narrative updates before checkpointing.
74	- A stale checkpoint can still be inspected, but automation can enforce freshness with `--check`.
75	- Repositories that intentionally hard-link canonical context must copy it to independent regular
76	  files before portable export.
77	- Semantic code-to-document freshness remains outside the current validator.
78	
79	## Validation
80	
81	- Missing, duplicate, empty, unknown, and out-of-order sections; CommonMark fence-length,
82	  blockquote, indented-code, and managed-evidence boundaries.
83	- Byte-identical repeated JSON, stale exit status, raw-byte digests, metadata exclusion, detached Git,
84	  warning deduplication, and progressive always/on-demand projection.
85	- Hard-link, symlink, containment, encoding, size, damaged Skill, and invalid-context rejection.
86	- Codex prompt-input discovery, Gemini Skill discovery, and fresh-session harness checks where the
87	  local authenticated tool is available.
88

1	# Tier 1 continuity pilot protocol
2	
3	- Status: Draft preregistration; execute only after repository/task fixtures and harness access are
4	  frozen in a committed revision
5	- Governing decision: `docs/decisions/0012-evidence-gates-before-continuity-expansion.md`
6	- Purpose: Determine whether the current Carrylog checkpoint shows enough behavioral signal to
7	  justify larger cross-harness, journaling, or compaction research
8	
9	## Scope
10	
11	This is a minimum viable maintainer-run pilot, not proof of universal continuity. It uses the current
12	checkpoint/resume product only. It does not require a session journal, delivery wrapper, transcript
13	parser, or Carrylog compactor.
14	
15	## Experimental matrix
16	
17	```text
18	repositories: 2
19	tasks per repository: 5
20	conditions: no-context, manual-handoff, carrylog-resume
21	harnesses: 2 authenticated harnesses from different supported surfaces
22	planned runs: 2 * 5 * 3 * 2 = 60
23	```
24	
25	Repository R1 may be Carrylog. R2 must differ materially in stack, size, ownership history, and task
26	shape. The exact commits or immutable fixture digests must be recorded before execution.
27	
28	The two harnesses should initially be Codex and Claude Code because they use distinct instruction and
29	Skill surfaces. If either is unavailable, substitution requires a committed protocol amendment before
30	results are generated.
31	
32	## Task families
33	
34	Each repository contributes one task from each family:
35	
36	1. reconstruct the current objective and safest next action;
37	2. continue a bounded implementation without repeating completed work;
38	3. preserve a protected architecture or compatibility decision;
39	4. avoid a previously failed approach and explain the relevant risk;
40	5. diagnose or verify state using the repository's required commands and limits.
41	
42	Every task fixture must define before execution:
43	
44	- relevant facts with fixed importance weights;
45	- prohibited reversals and repeated-work indicators;
46	- allowed clarification questions;
47	- expected verification behavior;
48	- a task-specific scoring rubric;
49	- sensitive facts that must not appear in output.
50	
51	## Conditions
52	
53	### No context
54	
55	Start the harness in the repository without a manual handoff or Carrylog resume envelope. Record any
56	project instructions the harness discovers automatically; this condition is not necessarily absence
57	of repository policy.
58	
59	### Manual handoff
60	
61	Provide a concise maintainer-written handoff that fits the same factual rubric. Freeze its exact bytes
62	before execution.
63	
64	### Carrylog resume
65	
66	Use the current validated checkpoint/resume workflow without adding an experimental journal or
67	semantic summary. Record artifact digests, discovery evidence, and any delivery evidence the harness
68	actually exposes.
69	
70	## Measures
71	
72	Report separately:
73	
74	- weighted relevant-fact reconstruction recall;
75	- weighted contradiction rate;
76	- prohibited reversal count;
77	- repeated-work count;
78	- unnecessary clarification count;
79	- task completion score under the preregistered rubric;
80	- input context size where observable;
81	- latency and estimated cost;
82	- evaluator confidence and unavailable evidence.
83	
84	Do not create a post-hoc composite utility score. Receipts and acknowledgements are delivery or
85	self-report evidence, not behavioral success.
86	
87	## Execution controls
88	
89	- Commit this protocol, task fixtures, rubrics, prompts, order-generation seed, and analysis script
90	  before the first scored run.
91	- Randomize or counterbalance condition and harness order within each task.
92	- Use fresh sessions and disable accidental conversation reuse.
93	- Record model and harness versions, context settings, repository commit, Carrylog commit, start time,
94	  exit status, and unavailable tools.
95	- Preserve sanitized raw visible output. Never collect hidden reasoning, credentials, or private
96	  provider stores.
97	- Score blind to condition where practical; record when blinding is impossible.
98	- Do not replace failed runs silently. Keep exclusions and reasons.
99

## Verification for `c9e8c2d`

### Resource boundaries

- **Per file:** configuration and each canonical context document are limited to **1 MiB = 1,048,576 bytes** per managed read (`src/commands/resume.ts:17`, `src/commands/resume.ts:207-223`).
- **Aggregate:** one portable-resume observation permits **8 MiB = 8,388,608 bytes**, including the configuration and **all** canonical documents—always-loaded and on-demand (`src/commands/resume.ts:18`, `src/commands/resume.ts:211-230`). The aggregate boundary is exercised by `tests/continuity.test.mjs:198-227` and documented at `docs/testing-strategy.md:80-81`.
- **Always-loaded:** `maxAlwaysCharacters` counts `content.length`, i.e. **JavaScript UTF-16 character/code units**, across all `load: always` documents, including the checkpoint (`src/validation/validate.ts:30-31`, `src/validation/validate.ts:85-97`). It is configurable from **1,000 through 100,000 character units**; the default is **16,000 character units** (`src/config/decode.ts:365-389`, `src/templates/defaults.ts:107-109`, `docs/configuration.md:99-108`). This is not a byte or tokenizer-token limit.

### Structural validity versus freshness

- **Structural validation** requires exactly one non-empty H2 section, in order, for: `Objective`, `Completed`, `Verification`, `Decisions`, `Risks`, and `Next action`. False headings inside managed evidence, fences, blockquotes, indented code, and supported HTML blocks are ignored (`src/continuity/checkpoint.ts:5-15`, `src/continuity/checkpoint.ts:116-174`; tests at `tests/continuity.test.mjs:48-134`).
- **Checkpoint freshness is separate:** resume compares the checkpoint’s managed Git evidence with a freshly rendered bounded Git observation. A mismatch sets `checkpoint.stale: true` and emits `W_CHECKPOINT_STALE`; it does **not** mean the six-section structure is invalid (`src/commands/resume.ts:91-132`). `resume --check` exits 1 for stale evidence, while the stale envelope remains inspectable (`docs/decisions/0010-portable-checkpoint-and-resume-boundary.md:28-44`, `tests/continuity.test.mjs:136-181`).
- Semantic code-to-document freshness is explicitly outside the validator (`docs/decisions/0010-portable-checkpoint-and-resume-boundary.md:74-77`).

### Local checks actually run

- `format:check` — passed; 64 files checked.
- Registered continuity tests — passed; **16/16**.
- Registered git-diff check — passed with exit 0 and no diff output.
